input: Write a thank-you note to my mentor

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing what specifically you are thanking them for shapes the entire content — general mentorship vs. a specific action, advice, or milestone changes everything.
The nature of the relationship (how close, how long, professional vs. personal) determines how familiar or formal the note should feel.
The occasion or trigger for the note (end of internship, after a big milestone, spontaneous gratitude) sets the emotional framing and urgency.
The delivery medium — handwritten card, email, LinkedIn message — dictates length, formatting, and style conventions.
The desired tone (warm and personal, professional and polished, brief and sincere) directly guides word choice and structure.
A target length or word count prevents the note from being too brief to feel genuine or too long for the medium.
Understanding the main feeling the user wants to leave their mentor with — inspired, appreciated, proud — defines what a great note actually achieves.

gold.taskTitle: Write a thank-you note to your mentor
gold.taskDescription: Draft a thank-you note addressed to the user's mentor, tailored to the right occasion, tone, length, and medium.

questions.title: What specific help or moment are you thanking them for?
questions.description: Identify the concrete action, advice, or support from the mentor that the note should acknowledge — e.g., career guidance, a referral, feedback on a project.

questions.title: How long and close is your relationship with them?
questions.description: Understand the depth of the relationship — e.g., a few months vs. several years, strictly professional vs. also a personal friendship — to calibrate familiarity.

questions.title: What occasion or event is prompting this note right now?
questions.description: Clarify the trigger for writing — wrapping up a program, landing a job, a recent conversation, or simply a spontaneous expression of gratitude.

questions.title: Will this be sent as an email, handwritten card, or something else?
questions.description: Determine the delivery format so the note is appropriately formatted and sized for the medium.

questions.title: Should the tone be warm and personal or polished and professional?
questions.description: Establish the stylistic register — heartfelt and conversational, crisp and formal, or somewhere in between.

questions.title: How long should the finished note roughly be?
questions.description: Set a target length — a few sentences, one short paragraph, or a fuller half-page — to match the user's expectations and the chosen medium.

questions.title: What is the one feeling you most want your mentor to walk away with?
questions.description: Pinpoint the emotional impact the user wants to create — that their effort mattered, that the user is proud of their growth, that the relationship is valued long-term.
